__comment: Phase 10b. What a student actually experiences, and what the platform is being asked to do. Every series here is an aggregate: by verdict, by language, by proctor signal TYPE, by sign-in failure code. There is no panel that can be narrowed to a person, because Prometheus is scraped by another host, kept for months and rendered on screens people photograph — a per-attempt proctor panel would be a per-student behavioural record in the least controlled datastore in the system.
title: REC Code — student experience

panels.title: Submit to verdict, as the student waits
panels.description: Observed where the student's wait ends, not where the judge's work ends: it includes the queue. SPEC's SLO is a p95 under 30s, which is where SubmissionLatencyP95High fires.

panels.title: Submissions per minute by language
panels.description: Load, and the shape of it. A language that suddenly stops appearing is usually a toolchain that stopped existing on the judge hosts after a rebuild.

panels.title: Open verdict streams
panels.description: Per web replica, which is correct for this one: the connections really are per replica, so two lines are two replicas and not one number counted twice.

panels.title: Proctor signals per minute, by type
panels.description: The type and nothing else. No signal here penalises anybody: the most the platform does automatically is flag an attempt for review and withhold it from the public leaderboard, and a human decides the rest.

panels.title: Refused sign-ins per minute, by reason
panels.description: Alerts above 100/min (FailedLoginBurst). `rate-limited` climbing while `credentials` stays flat is the limiter working: a run against one account is refused before the password is ever checked.
